thread:
Maya Chen: FYI customer ask from Acme Robotics — they want Harrier-9B reduced to fit a single 16GB on-prem GPU for inference. Target: <=16GB RAM, p99 <120ms @batch=1, must pass our smoke quality suite before we ship. Can we triage?
Liam O'Connor: do they need int8 or 4-bit? quality tradeoffs matter here.
Maya Chen: they asked for 'as small as possible with acceptable quality' — open to Q4 if perf looks good.
Anika Gupta: Proposed quick triage checklist:
- verify tokenizer + hf model artefacts exist
- run baseline eval (FP16) on acme_smoke prompts
- run quant sweep: Q8/Q4 + per-channel vs per-tensor where supported
- measure memory (peak) and p99 latency on target hardware image
- run quality regression vs baseline (BLEU/ROUGE + curated smoke failures)
- canary deploy on dedicated pool, monitor token-level errors and latency
I'll add checklist items to the intake ticket.
Owen Park: need ephemeral infra for the sweep. How long do you think?
Anika Gupta: ~48–72h for sweep + initial regressions assuming GPU availability.
Samir Patel: I can own smoke evals and initial regressions. Where's the prompt set?
Maya Chen: path: s3://redwood-evals/acme/harrier_smoke_v1.jsonl — includes 150 prompts (safety, instructions, code, multi-step).
Samir Patel: ack. will start baseline run on FP16 first. please tag the dataset in the ticket.
onboard-bot: Ephemeral cluster created: harrier-9b-quant-sweep (gpu:1 a5000, expires in 72h) — link: https://infra.redwood/ephemeral/harrier-9b-quant-sweep
Liam O'Connor: quick note — for Q4 we should try GPTQ-style per-channel calibration. also try out 8-bit LLM.int8() path to compare.
Samir Patel: command I'll run:
```
# baseline
python eval_runner.py --model s3://models/harrier-9b/fp16 --prompts s3://redwood-evals/acme/harrier_smoke_v1.jsonl --out /tmp/harrier_fp16.jsonl
# q4 quantize
./tools/quantize --model s3://models/harrier-9b/fp16 --bits 4 --calib-data s3://redwood-evals/acme/harrier_calib.jsonl --out /tmp/harrier_q4.bin
```
Samir Patel: will post perf numbers + quality diffs in the ticket.
Maya Chen: priority P1 for this customer (they're in pilot). But operationally P2 for engineering queue — need realistic ETA.
Owen Park: I'll queue up a dedicated CI slot for the canary once we have a Q candidate. Assign infra@ticket.
Anika Gupta: acceptance criteria suggestion:
- relative quality delta <= 3% on core metrics + no critical failures in safety checks
- peak memory <= 16GB on their runtime image
- p99 latency <120ms @batch=1 on a5000 equivalent
- rollout plan: canary 1% -> 10% -> full with automatic rollback on regressions
If those look good we can include as 'supported variant' in model catalog.
Samir Patel: starting runs now, will post first FP16 baseline by EOD UTC.
Maya Chen: thank you — please @me on major regressions. :eyes: :rocket:
Liam O'Connor: one more thing — add a note about tokenizer fast vs slow issues. Harrier had different BOS tokens in dev sync last month.
Maya Chen: noted, will include in ticket.
Samir Patel: update 03: baseline done. avg tokens/sec 45, p99 95ms FP16. uploading results to ticket. next: Q8 then Q4 sweep.
Maya Chen: great, leaving action items: Samir run quant sweep (owner), Anika write acceptance + rollout steps (owner), Owen reserve canary infra (owner). ETA tentative 3 business days for initial verdict.
onboard-bot: Ticket created: #IN-4821 — Harrier-9B Acme edge quant intake. Assignees: Samir Patel, Anika Gupta, Owen Park.
Maya Chen: closing this thread for now — continue updates on IN-4821. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
